description: The fraction of integers surviving all sieves decreases as N grows — empirically ~1.9x per additional bit. For N=45, 0.0506% survive; for N=72, ~0.0127%. This self-improving property is analogous to concentration of measure: as N increases, random Collatz trajectories are increasingly likely to descend.
mathematical_formalization: S(N) = #{n < 2^N surviving all sieves} / 2^N ~ C * alpha^N with alpha ~ 0.95. Heuristic: each bit adds an independent descent chance. The CLT applied to the random walk S_k = 306k - 485f_k predicts exponential decay of survival.
analogical_connections: Concentration of measure in high dimensions
implementation_hypothesis: Adaptive algorithm: run calibration for small N, estimate S(N), choose optimal (A, B) parameters. For larger N, increase A from 6 to 10+, as recursive step produces fewer survivors per work unit.
experiment_seed: Run complete algorithm for N=35..55, plot S(N) on semi-log scale. Fit exponential model. Extrapolate to N=72,77,80.
